In a sector as competitive as foodservice, spontaneity is not a strategy. To gain visibility, build customer loyalty and maximize sales, you need to anticipate and plan your highlights, punctuate your marketing campaigns, and capitalize on relevant chestnuts.

This 2026 marketing calendar dedicated to the restaurant industry provides you with a complete roadmap: month by month, essential dates, themes to exploit, and opportunities to seize. Whether you're an independent, chain or franchised restaurateur, this guide will help you structure your actions, avoid dead time, and give meaning to each of your communications.

How to use this calendar to boost your restaurant

You now have a 2026 marketing calendar tailored to the foodservice industry. But a calendar without action remains a dead letter: it's in the execution that the difference is made.

Here's what we recommend to make the most of this calendar:

  1. Select your priority highlights
    Not all events are worth activating. Choose 4 to 6 highlights for your concept: those in affinity with your customers, your offer or your positioning.
  2. Turn ideas into content and offers
    For each selected highlight, create offers (special menus, promotions, themed cards) and content (posts, stories, emailing). Combine them with a distribution calendar.
  3. Plan then adjust
    Create your annual editorial schedule now, with milestones for creation, validation and distribution. But stay flexible: monitor feedback, trends, performance, and adapt.
  4. Systematically measure
    For each campaign, define indicators (additional sales, opening rates, engagement, traffic). Analyze what works, and capitalize.
  5. Capitalize and recycle
    Don't start from scratch every year. Reuse and improve content, adjust visuals, update offers based on feedback.

This calendar is not a sacred to-do list, but a strategic framework. It's up to you to make it lively, relevant and aligned with your brand.
